top_signals.title: Saudi Arabia Restarts Red Sea Crude Oil Loadings
top_signals.summary: Saudi Arabia has restarted crude oil loadings at the Yanbu port on the Red Sea after the East-West pipeline resumed partial service, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing vessel-tracking data and trade sources. Saudi Arabia shut down the East-West onshore pipeline for two weeks following drone attacks that damaged pumping stations on September 10. The pipeline that helps the Kingdom bypass the Strait of Hormuz resumed partial service last Thursday, but full resumption of flows of about 4 million barrels per day (bpd) would likely take weeks. top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin gives back gains as long-term holder supply keeps $85K out of reach
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin failed to make another run at $85,000 as sellers held the line above current levels, while surging US bond yields weighed on stocks and precious metals.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Patriarch Says Listing May Limit Tata Sons’ Role as Backstop
top_signals.summary: Founding-family patriarch Noel Tata said a public listing could constrain Tata Sons Pvt.’s ability to support group firms in trouble, making his case in a rare public interview nearly two weeks after a boardroom fight erupted at one of India’s largest conglomerates.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: JPMorgan, Ford to Invest Billions in Michigan Manufacturing
top_signals.summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Ford Motor Co. are helping launch a new program to bolster production in the state of Michigan. The bank and automaker will help suppliers in the program. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, Ford CEO Jim Farley and Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer speak exclusively to Bloomberg's David Westin in Detroit.  (Source: Bloomberg)
